title: Daughter Mubashra's school
takeaway: A good school feels like a mother's lap.
scene: The heading says 'At daughter Mubashra's request'. Mubashra asked her father to write a poem for her school, and it celebrates the school and its teachers. A note at the end says the full poem was long, so only part of it could be printed.

original: رنگ رنگ دے مہکدے پھل ایتھے، کھڑی ہوئی اے عجب گلزار ایتھے
ہاسے چمکدے موہناں تے نور بن کے خشیاں ونڈدی پھرے بہار ایتھے
transliteration: Rang rang de mehakde phull ethe, khiri hoi ae ajab gulzaar ethe
Haase chamakde mohnaan te noor ban ke, khushiyaan vandi phire bahaar ethe
translation: Here, fragrant flowers of every colour; here, a wonderful garden is in bloom.
Laughter shines like light on lovely faces; here, spring goes around handing out joy.
couplets.story: The school is like a garden full of flowers of every colour. Those flowers are the students. Their laughing faces shine, and happiness is everywhere, as if spring itself were handing it out.

original: تارو بحر کمال تے حکمتاں دے علم دفن دے شاہ اسوار ایتھے
ایہہ ذیشان مینار اے روشنی دا نظر علم دے آن انوار ایتھے
transliteration: Taaroo behr-e-kamaal te hikmataan de, ilm-o-fann de shaah-savaar ethe
Eh zeeshaan minaar ae roshni da, nazar ilm de aan anvaar ethe
translation: Here are swimmers in the ocean of excellence and wisdom, champion riders of knowledge and skill.
This is a splendid tower of light; here you can see the radiance of learning.
couplets.story: The teachers here are experts, like strong swimmers in an ocean of knowledge. The school is like a tall lighthouse, shining the light of learning.

original: آن والیاں نویاں سہیلیاں نوں اسی جی آیاں سارے آکھدے ہاں
سچی گل اے ماں دی گود وانگوں تسیں پاؤ گے رج کے پیار ایتھے
transliteration: Aan vaaliyaan naviyaan saheliyaan nu, asi ji aayaan saare aakhde haan
Sachchi gall ae, maan di god vaangon, tusi paaoge raj ke pyaar ethe
translation: To all the new friends who are joining, we all say: welcome!
It's true: like a mother's lap, you'll find all the love you need here.
couplets.story: The students welcome every new girl who joins. They promise that this school is like a mother's lap: you'll find plenty of love here.

original: سربراہ نیں مسز چوہان ساڈے جیہڑے اپنی آپ مثال ہے نیں
جنہاں فہم فراست تے علم سیتی قائم کیتا اے سوہنا معیار ایتھے
transliteration: Sarbaraah nain Mrs. Chauhan saade, jehre apni aap misaal hai nain
Jinhaan fehm firaasat te ilm seeti qaaim keeta ae sohna miyaar ethe
translation: Our head is Mrs. Chauhan, who is an example all by herself,
and who, with understanding, insight and learning, has set a fine standard here.
couplets.story: The headmistress, Mrs. Chauhan, is a role model. Through her wisdom and knowledge she has made it an excellent school.

original: مسز رانا کردار گفتار دلوں بڑے اچے مقام تے نظر آون نیں
دھڑکن وانگ اوہ دلاں دے وچ دھڑکن سب دکھاں دے سانجھی غم خوار ایتھے
transliteration: Mrs. Rana kirdaar guftaar dilon bare uchche muqaam te nazar aavan nain
Dharkan vaang oh dilaan de vich dharkan, sab dukhaan de saanjhi gham-khaar ethe
translation: Mrs. Rana, in character, speech and heart, stands at a very high level.
She beats like a heartbeat in everyone's heart; here she shares in all our sorrows.
couplets.story: Mrs. Rana is good-hearted and speaks kindly. She's so close to the students it's as if she lives in their hearts, and she's there for them whenever they're sad.

original: طالبات دے دلاں وچ گھر کیتا سب نوں مان ایں مسز اقبال اتے
جہدے آہر پیار اخلاق سیتی علم فن ادب تے آیا نکھار ایتھے
transliteration: Taalibaat de dilaan vich ghar keeta, sab nu maan ain Mrs. Iqbal utte
Jihde aahar pyaar ikhlaaq seeti ilm fann adab te aaya nikhaar ethe
translation: She has made a home in the students' hearts; everyone is proud of Mrs. Iqbal,
whose effort, love and good manners have made learning, skills and literature flourish here.
couplets.story: Mrs. Iqbal has a place in every student's heart, and everyone is proud of her. Her hard work, kindness and good manners have helped learning and the arts grow.

original: اس علم دے گلشن نوں یا مولا صدقہ نبی دا سدا آباد رکھیں
ایسے طراں احمدؔ خشیاں رونقاں دا لگا رہے ہمیش دربار ایتھے
transliteration: Is ilm de gulshan nu ya Maula, sadqa Nabi da, sada aabaad rakheen
Ise taraan Ahmad khushiyaan raunqaan da laga rahe hamesh darbaar ethe
translation: O Lord, for the sake of the Prophet, keep this garden of learning always flourishing.
Ahmad prays that a court of joy and liveliness may always be held here.
couplets.story: He ends with a prayer. Dear God, for the sake of the Prophet, keep this school full of life forever. May it always be a happy, busy place.

deeper: Only the last couplet is a prayer, but it frames the whole poem. The poet asks God, 'for the sake of the Prophet', to keep the school flourishing. In Islam, a place where people learn is a blessing, so praying for a school is a natural thing to do.
why: A loving poem a father wrote because his daughter asked. It honours the women teachers who ran her school.
prompt: What makes a school feel like 'a mother's lap'? Which teacher made you feel welcome?

editorNote.original: نوٹ۔ معذرت نال ایہہ نظم کافی لمی اے جگہ دی قلت موجب ساری پیش نہ کیتی جا سکی
editorNote.translation: Note: With apologies, this poem is quite long, and for lack of space it could not be printed in full.

notes: The school is not named in this extract; it may be the same Gojra girls' school as page 77.
